thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Anduril Industries (SWE, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Two bars in sequence: an eligibility bar (U.S. Person / export-control / clearance eligibility on many roles, applied at application stage) and then a fairly conventional but mission-probing technical bar (coding incl. C++ debugging reports, design, and repeated 'why Anduril' motivation checks in candidate reports). Candidates who cannot clear the first bar should not spend prep time on the second.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Public postings describe the roles a company is currently trying to fill, not the people it actually hired; interview-prep and review sites are self-selected candidate reports; no licensed population dataset (PDL/Coresignal-class) was available for this record, so no school/employer/major shares are stated. Anduril-specific: posting mirrors may lag Greenhouse; clearance/U.S.-Person requirements vary BY ROLE - some roles list Secret eligibility, others TS/SCI, and non-controlled roles may differ, so per-posting verification is mandatory.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Anduril Industries says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: U.S. Person status is an explicit requirement on sourced SWE postings 'due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities' Many roles require eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance (Secret on one sourced posting; Top Secret SCI on the scientific SWE posting, active TS/SCI listed as desired there) The application asks directly whether the candidate will require sponsorship now or in the future (e.g. H-1B) - combined with export-control rules, non-U.S.-Persons should assume most SWE roles are closed and verify role-by-role Transcripts are requested early in the application process on sourced postings to assess coursework fit (redaction of non-technical info permitted; unofficial transcripts acceptable) Applications disclose third-party pre-employment risk/integrity screening (sanctions/watchlist/adverse-media checks) as part of the process Mission motivation is a repeated interview theme in candidate reports ('why Anduril' asked across rounds) - anecdotal but consistent
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: Direct application via Greenhouse (official board) — See route details.
Second: Recruiter outreach / referral — See route details.
Third: University/new-grad SWE postings — See route details.

Your gap analysis (highest-leverage fix first: experience):
- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§3.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — Two bars in sequence: an eligibility bar (U.S. Person / export-control / clearance eligibility on many roles, applied at application stage) and then a fairly conventional but mission-probing technical bar (coding incl. C++ debugging reports, design, and repeated 'why Anduril' motivation checks in candidate reports). Candidates who cannot clear the first bar should not spend prep time on the second. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — Continuous, posting-driven hiring (Greenhouse board) rather than a published annual cohort calendar in the sources found; defence programme demand drives waves that are not publicly scheduled. | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next thirty days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Anduril Industries on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§3.3). (by 2026-10-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-10-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-10-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
- Be in the application pool for Anduril Industries's main entry window with the ladder rung, the project write-up and the referral conversations already done — not started.
- If the direct route misses, take the highest adjacent rung this CIR names and re-aim with a year of signal (the risks-and-alternatives route in this thesis).

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

Timeline and key dates: Continuous, posting-driven hiring (Greenhouse board) rather than a published annual cohort calendar in the sources found; defence programme demand drives waves that are not publicly scheduled. (as of 2026-10-12; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §3.3).

Risks and alternatives: ELIGIBILITY FIRST: if you are not a U.S. Person, or would need H-1B sponsorship, most Anduril SWE roles are closed by export-control law - the application asks both questions directly. Do not advise anyone to misstate this (Doc 3 s3.2: never fabricate). Clearance timelines are outside the candidate's control and can extend offers by months - plan finances/timing accordingly (general reported norm, labeled). Onsite intensity: at least some postings require 5-days-per-week onsite presence - confirm per role. Defence work itself is a values decision for the candidate: some strong engineers opt out; surface this neutrally and early. Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.

Want me to execute? I can build the coffee-chat target list from these routes, tailor your resume to this record's revealed screens (truthfully — only what you have actually done), and set the plan's reminders. Say the word and I start with the list.
